description: Use when the user asks whether a specific broadband provider is down, having problems or has an outage, e.g. 'is BT down?' or 'Virgin Media not working'. Returns what that provider's FindBroadband page shows: the status and its headline, the current incidents and the most recent past ones in the provider's own words with the places they named, a day by day picture of the last 30 days and links. Quote the headline and the provider's words as given rather than rewording them. When status_based_on is public_reports we can't read the provider's own status page: Down means people are reporting problems, which the provider hasn't confirmed, and Working fine means nobody is reporting problems, not that the provider has said all is well. Never tell the user their own line is or isn't affected: say what has been reported and where, and point them to the provider's status page or the provider if they are still offline. The status is for the provider's home broadband. When scope_note is present, give it with the status: it says what the page tracks and where to check the provider's mobile network or TV, which a user with no mobile signal may be asking about.

provider.description: The broadband provider the user means, as they said it (e.g. 'BT', 'Virgin Media', 'zen'). Free text is fine.

name: get_provider_outage_status

last_report_at.description: For public_reports entries: when the last public report came in. People stopped reporting problems around then; the provider never confirmed a fault or a fix.

title: Is this broadband provider down?
